extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and USPTO disciplinary staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline (exclusion/disbarment) by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when a practitioner has been disciplined by a state authority. Includes notice, default consequences, aggravating facts, and administrative consequences (publication, dissociation from customer numbers, notification obligations, duties while excluded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and 35 U.S.C. § 32, the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline (including exclusion) when a practitioner has been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 as the statutory and regulatory basis for imposing reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline is predicated on violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h): having been disbarred (or otherwise disciplined) by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states Respondent's reciprocal discipline is predicated on her violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), having been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a state (disbarment by the Supreme Court of Georgia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (service and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must send a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' by certified mail and provide the respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the state discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the Notice and Order was sent by certified mail (receipt numbers provided) and afforded 40 days to respond; it was also published for two consecutive weeks in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order must be published in the Official Gazette (the Notice here was published for two consecutive weeks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was published for two consecutive weeks in the Official Gazette; the Final Order also directs the OED Director to publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion and its basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default and deemed-admitted facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file a timely response may result in default; when respondent fails to respond, there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and the facts alleged by the state may be deemed admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Respondent failed to file a response, the Order determined no genuine issue of material fact existed and reciprocal exclusion was appropriate; the Georgia Supreme Court deemed facts admitted due to default after failure to file a Notice of Rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of misconduct supporting discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific misconduct alleged that supports discipline includes: failing on numerous occasions to communicate with a client, failing to respond to the client's attorney in a pending lawsuit to settle the case, failing to respond to the bankruptcy trustee, not refunding unearned fees, being sanctioned and terminated as counsel by the bankruptcy court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette Notice summarizes the misconduct admitted in the state proceeding as the factual basis for disbarment and reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggravating factors justifying harsher sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggravating circumstances include acting willfully (e.g., collecting a fee and then 'abandoning' the client's legal matter), acting with selfish motive, substantial experience in the practice of law, prior disciplinary history, and failure to respond adequately to a Notice of Investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State's Investigative Panel found these aggravating factors and, together with the respondent's default, concluded disbarment was the appropriate sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate discipline following state disbarment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline imposed by the USPTO can mirror the state sanction — here, exclusion from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly excluded the Respondent from practice before the USPTO commencing on the date of the Order, identical to the state-imposed disbarment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required publication content for Notice of Exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Exclusion published by the OED Director must identify the respondent (name, city/state, registration number), state the disciplinary finding (basis for exclusion, e.g., violation of § 11.804(h) predicated on state disbarment), and summarize the factual and procedural bases for the discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides the text of a Notice of Exclusion describing the respondent, registration number, the basis for the exclusion, and a summary of admitted facts and aggravating findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for it to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order instructs the OED Director to provide such notice as part of the administrative steps following exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of excluded practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent who is excluded must comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded from practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order requires Respondent to comply with § 11.58 duties, though it does not reproduce that section's text; practitioners must consult § 11.58 for specific obligations (e.g., notice to clients, withdrawal, safekeeping of client property, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs administrative dissociation to prevent the excluded person from using prior electronic credentials in USPTO systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on applying for or obtaining Customer Numbers while excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall the respondent's name be added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order bars any attempt to obtain access via Customer Numbers or to be added to existing Customer Numbers until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides the FOIA Reading Room link (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp) as the location where disciplinary decisions are published for public review.
